newsitem.title: USA: Mobil had record quarterly operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Mobil had record quarterly operating profit.

text.p: Mobil Corp Monday reported fourth quarter 1996 operating income of $879 million pointing out this was the highest for any quarter in its history.

Operating earnings per common share were $2.20 compared with $1.89 in 1995, an increase of 16 percent and well above the First Call consensus estimate of $1.97. Including special items, net income for the quarter was $676 million, or $1.68 per share.
Annual operating income topped $3 billion for the first time, reaching a record $3.10 billion, the company said. On a per-share basis, operating profits of $7.72 were up nine percent.
Including special items, full year net income was $2,964 million, or $7.38 per share.

Earnings growth resulted from strong crude oil and natural gas prices, increased international production of crude oil and natural gas, higher petroleum product sales, and expense reductions, the company's statement said.

In 1996, the company said, "we were able to grow volumes significantly in all sectors, while reducing per barrel expenses by about 10 percent. Since we are in a very competitive industry that is subject to significant price volatility, we must continue these efforts. We are not counting on a continuation of the current high oil and gas prices or an overall improvement in business conditions."

It said these factors more than offset expenses related to increased volumes and growth programs, opportunity losses related to hydrocarbon hedging, and weaker industry margins in the international downstream and petrochemical businesses where the company has a substantial presence.
"Our outlook for these businesses continues to be favorable for the longer term," it said while declining to elaborate on the spread over consensus expectations.
Additionally, Mobil said, "results were hurt by increased downtime in our refineries and reduced chemical plant operating reliability. We are addressing these areas and expect to show improvement.
"The absence of income from divested chemical businesses and the expiration of the tax holiday for our petrochemicals joint venture in Saudi Arabia also had negative impacts."

All of the programs required to support the $1.3 billion reduction in costs announced over the past few years were in place by the end of 1996 and contributed, as expected, to the increase in earnings, Mobil said.

Mobil said the $203 million difference between its record operating profits and net income reflects charges of $145 million for previously announced start-up costs for Mobil's downstream European joint venture with British Petroleum Co Plc and $69 million for the FAS 121 write-down of a Gulf of Mexico property, partly offset by $11 million of various net favorable items, mostly inventory adjustments.
During the latest quarter, Mobil said, its benefits from the crude price increase were reduced somewhat due to the weakening of prices for California heavy crudes relative to light crudes.
These heavy crudes make up about 40 percent of Mobil's U.S. production.

Growth in production was due to the streaming of a new field in Equatorial Guinea, new production from existing fields in Nigeria, higher production in Indonesia to meet contract demand, and new production from Ampolex and the Tengiz field. Production also started from the Qatargas liquefied natural gas project in November.
In spite of higher U.S. refinery downtime during the fourth quarter, combined gasoline and distillate production was an all-time high for a quarter, Mobil said.

Margins in Australia and Japan were weaker as crude prices increased and competitive pressures precluded recovery of these higher costs. Benefits from higher refining margins at Mobil's Singapore refinery were more than offset by lower paraxylene margins. Higher petroleum product sales in Asia-Pacific contributed favorably to earnings.
